gloss: temple town; town around a temple or shrine

definitions.gloss: temple town; town that developed around a major temple or shrine
definitions.explanation: A settlement that grew up around a prominent temple or shrine, with shops, inns, and residences catering to pilgrims and visitors. Many such towns still retain their historical character today.

examples.japanese: {善光寺|ぜんこうじ}の{門前町|もんぜんまち}を{歩|ある}いた。
examples.english: I walked through the temple town of Zenkōji.

examples.japanese: この{通|とお}りは{昔|むかし}からの{門前町|もんぜんまち}の{雰囲気|ふんいき}が{残|のこ}っている。
examples.english: This street still retains the atmosphere of an old temple town.

examples.japanese: {門前町|もんぜんまち}には{参拝客|さんぱいきゃく}{向|む}けの{土産物屋|みやげものや}や{食堂|しょくどう}が{並|なら}んでいる。
examples.english: The temple town is lined with souvenir shops and restaurants for visitors.

notes:
Composed of {門前|もんぜん} (in front of the gate) + {町|まち} (town). Historically, these towns developed organically around major temples and shrines as pilgrims needed lodging, food, and supplies. Famous examples include the towns around {善光寺|ぜんこうじ} in Nagano, {伊勢神宮|いせじんぐう} in Mie, and {成田山|なりたさん} in Chiba.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {門前町|もんぜんまち}を{散策|さんさく}する: to stroll through a temple town
- {門前町|もんぜんまち}の{名物|めいぶつ}: local specialty of a temple town
- {古|ふる}い{門前町|もんぜんまち}: old temple town

RELATED WORDS:
- {城下町|じょうかまち}: castle town — a town that developed around a feudal lord's castle
- {宿場町|しゅくばまち}: post town — a town along a historical highway that served as a rest stop
- {門前|もんぜん}: in front of the gate — also appears in the proverb {門前|もんぜん}の{小僧|こぞう}{習|なら}わぬ{経|きょう}を{読|よ}む (a boy living near a temple can recite sutras without studying them)
